skill_traces.query:
Nate: Hey Joanna, what a wild week! My game tournament got pushed back, so I tried out some cooking. Look at this homemade coconut ice cream! The sprinkles kinda changed the color this time around.
Joanna: Hey Nate, that looks yummy! Wish I could try it, but I can't right now. How did the last game tournament go?
Nate: Hey Joanna, thanks! Tough tournament, didn't make it to the finals. But that's okay, I'll get 'em next time!
Joanna: Aww, bummer! But the important thing is to stay positive. So, what's your next move in the gaming world?
Nate: Thanks Joanna! Staying positive is key. I'm thinking of joining a new gaming team after this next tourney - I've had a few offers, but I haven't decided yet. It's gonna be a big step, but I'm ready for a shake up.
Joanna: Sounds great, Nate! Making a switch could open up new opportunities. Wishing you luck with picking the right team!
Nate: Thanks, Joanna! I really appreciate it. It's a big decision, but I'm excited for what the future holds. How about you? Anything exciting happening on your end?
Joanna: Yup! I worked hard on another script and eventually created a plan for getting it made into a movie. It was a ton of work but satisfying. I pitched it to some producers yesterday and they really liked it. It gave me a big confidence boost!
Nate: Congrats on the chance to pitch your script - super impressive. Proud of you!
Joanna: Appreciate you, Nate! Your support and encouragement mean a lot to me. I feel like I just can't stop writing write now!
Nate: Anytime. What're you working on in that notebook? Anything cool?
Joanna: Hey Nate, I'm working on a new project - a suspenseful thriller set in a small Midwestern town. It's been a great creative outlet for me. How about you? Do you have any projects you're working on?
Nate: Yeah actually - creating gaming content for YouTube. It's a cool way to entertain folks and satisfy my video game cravings at the same time when there aren't any tourneys going on.
Joanna: Wow, that's a cool idea! What inspired you to start making gaming videos?
Nate: Hey Joanna, I'm a big fan of them and thought it would be a fun idea to start making them myself. I'm hoping to share my love of gaming and connect with others who enjoy it too.
Joanna: Way to go, Nate! Making videos and connecting with people about gaming - that's awesome! You'll do great!
Nate: Thanks Joanna! Appreciate the support. It's new to me but I'm excited to get started!
Joanna: Make sure you watch other peoples videos first so you get a handle on what your audience likes! That way your videos don't flop when you post them.
Nate: Already doing that, but thanks for the advice!
Joanna: No worries, Nate! It's great to support each other in reaching our goals. On another note, check out this pic I got a while back!
Nate: Wow, that sunset pic looks incredible! What inspired you to take that photo?
Joanna: Thanks, Nate! I took that pic on a hike last summer near Fort Wayne. The sunset and the surrounding beauty were just incredible. It was an awesome reminder of nature's beauty.
Nate: That sounds incredible! Nature truly has a way of reminding us to appreciate the beauty around us, and moments like those really stay with you. These critters also make me appreciate life's little joys. And guess what? I got them a new friend!
Joanna: Wow, what made you get a third?
Nate: Turtles really bring me joy and peace. They have such an effect on us - best buddies ever! I saw another at a pet store and just hade to get him. The tank is big enough now for three, so I figured why not!
Joanna: Wow! It's always a shock where life will take us next! I bet just last week you would have never thought you would be getting a third turtle this year!
Nate: You got that right, but I'm very happy with the descision and wouldn't have it any other way.
Joanna: Can I come over sometime and watch you play with them? From a distance I mean, since I'm allergic.
Nate: Definitely! I'd love to have you over again. Maybe we can watch one of your movies together or go to the park!
Joanna: For sure! I'd love to do either of those things with you!
Nate: Sounds good. Well I'll make sure I give the turtles a bath before you get here so they're ready to play.
Joanna: Alright, see you tomorrow!
Nate: Bye Joanna!

selected.rerank_reason: Joanna mentions her inspiration for the movie script and Nate discusses his motivation for creating gaming content, which involves plans and inspirations.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Photo-Sharing Events
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message presents an object or result with visual language like 'Here are...' or explicitly mentions sharing a photo, during extraction.
content: When a message uses presentation phrasing such as 'Here are...', 'Check out...', 'This is a photo of...', or 'Attached is...' to introduce something, record that the speaker shared a photo of that item, even if the word 'photo' does not appear.

If the speaker explicitly mentions sharing, sending, or showing a picture/photo/image, create an event memory that records the sharing action and the described content (e.g., subject or creator of the picture).
Preserve the literal object named in the message (e.g., picture) — do not replace it with an inferred object such as a bookshelf, item, or possession.
Keep the sharing act within the same event memory as the other facts from that message; do not summarize away the visual sharing.
Only include facts explicitly stated; do not convert a shared picture into an ownership claim unless ownership is directly stated.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Suggestions
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message contains explicit advice, suggestions, or recommendations from one participant to another, extract them as memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, suggestions, and recommendations as memory-worthy. Capture the advisor, the recipient, the advised action, and the source message.
Preserve all distinct pieces of advice and their qualifiers; do not collapse or omit details. Tentative phrasing still counts.
Represent as an event or relationship memory; create at most one candidate per distinct piece of advice.
Stop after capturing the stated advice; do not infer outcomes or expand into related topics.

nearby_not_selected.name: Capture likely deceased from euphemistic absence language
nearby_not_selected.description: During extraction, when a speaker describes someone with euphemistic absence language (e.g., 'will never be able to...', 'I miss him/her here') that strongly implies death, use this guidance.
content: When a statement euphemistically implies a person has died without explicitly saying so, also extract the implied state that the person is likely deceased, in addition to the literal statement.
Record the inference with an appropriate hedge (e.g., 'likely deceased') because the speaker did not state it directly; do not assert cause, date, or circumstances of death.
Stop after capturing the likely-deceased state and the literal content; do not extrapolate further details about the person or the relationship.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Concrete Events over Interpretive Summaries
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states a concrete event with specific participants and timing inside a broader narrative.
content: When a message states a concrete event such as receiving/giving an object at a specific age or time, create a separate event memory recording the giver, recipient, object, and timing.
If the same sentence also contains a broader statement, keep that derived state only as an additional memory; never let it replace the concrete event fact.
Ensure every concrete noun phrase appears in the memory content.
